manifest.research_question: Research verified literature where user next-item behavior, hyperbolic geometry and generative semantic IDs intersect.

sources.title: Recommender Systems with Generative Retrieval
sources.verification_basis: arXiv full-text preprint; title and identifier resolve at the canonical arXiv record.
sources.exact_overlap: Directly addresses generative recommendation/retrieval using learned semantic IDs (RQ-VAE item codes) and user interaction histories, including sequential next-item recommendation. The paper does not establish use of hyperbolic geometry.

sources.title: Hyperbolic Representation Learning for Collaborative Filtering
sources.verification_basis: Not included: title-level candidate could not be independently verified to a stable bibliographic record in this run. No claims are attributed to it.
sources.exact_overlap: Unverified lead only; excluded from evidence and conclusions.

behavior_problem_candidates.candidate: Modeling the next item as a behavior-conditioned generation problem over semantic item codes, while using hyperbolic geometry to represent hierarchical or long-tail structure in the item/code space.
behavior_problem_candidates.behavior_problem: Given a user's observed interaction sequence, generate/rank the next item; investigate whether sparse histories and tail-item transitions are better represented when item relationships have hierarchical structure.
basis: Recommender Systems with Generative Retrieval (arXiv:2305.05065) supports behavior-conditioned semantic-ID generation; it does not support the hyperbolic component.
behavior_problem_candidates.decision: Treat as a research gap/hypothesis, not as an existing method or demonstrated result.

limitations: No independently verified full-text source found in this pass that explicitly combines all three elements: user next-item behavior, hyperbolic geometry, and generative semantic IDs.
The verified source establishes only the behavior-plus-generative-semantic-ID pair; hyperbolic geometry must not be inferred from hierarchical semantic codes.
The unverified hyperbolic recommendation lead is explicitly excluded from evidence; its metadata and overlap remain UNKNOWN.
A full-text label indicates an accessible full-text preprint exists, not that every claim has been independently replicated.
No unseen future/test interactions or prior-candidate prompts were used.
